title: Crestline - Semantic Search Workshop
summary: 40min product walkthrough of Redwood hosted embeddings + reranking endpoints. Focus on integration patterns, latency vs. cost tradeoffs, Console walkthrough for Optimize suggestions, and a short live demo sending batch queries. Customer wants pilot for 100k docs and strict PII redaction needs. Agreed to run a small benchmark and follow up with pricing and security docs.
topics: Architecture: embedding + kNN retrieval + reranker flow
Console: per-route latency/cost dashboards and Optimize suggestions
Quality vs cost: quantization and batching tradeoffs
Security: PII redaction, KMS, audit logs, SOC2
Pilot scope: 100k documents, 2 region latency targets
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-14 16:00 PDT | Duration: ~54m | Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Rachel Gomez (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Mark Huang (Crestline HoS), Lina Torres (Eng Mgr), Devon Price (ML Eng), Priya (Intern)

[00:00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time, um, from Redwood side it's Samir and Rachel and Jordan. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:06] Mark: Good, thanks. Excited to see how this could help our search stack.
[00:00:10] Samir: Awesome. Quick agenda — we'll do a brief recap of your goals, then a walkthrough of the embeddings + reranker flow using the hosted endpoints, show the Console Optimize suggestions, and finish with a short live batch demo and next steps. Any additions?
[00:00:22] Lina: Maybe if we have time, could you show how prefix caching or batching affects latency? We've been tripping over tail latency spikes.
[00:00:28] Rachel: Absolutely we'll cover KV caching, batching, and tip on sequence lengths.
[00:00:33] Samir: Cool, Mark — can you quickly restate the success criteria? I have a note but want to confirm.
[00:00:38] Mark: Yeah so primary is relevance uplift — we want +10 to click-through on top-3 results on content search. Secondary is latency under 150ms p95 for our public web queries, and third is data safety — anything with PII needs to be redacted and not leave our tenant. We also want a clear unit-cost estimate for 100k docs.
[00:00:54] Jordan: Thanks. A couple clarifying Qs from our side: What's your current vector store and retrieval stack?
[00:00:59] Devon: We're running FAISS on-prem for embeddings store, nightly re-embeds with a transformer from last year, and the reranker today is a lightweight in-house BERT for reordering top-20. We tried a dense-rerank but it was too slow.
[00:01:12] Rachel: Great context. Today's demo assumes using Redwood hosted embeddings to reduce embedding ops cost and the reranker hosted too, so you'd keep FAISS or swap to a cloud-managed vector DB — both are supported.
[00:01:24] Samir: Ok jumping into the flow — slide 4 of our deck, but I'll also show the Console. The simple flow: client calls /embeddings to index documents, store vectors in your vector DB, then at query time call embeddings for query, run approximate kNN, then call /rerank endpoint with top-K candidates. The reranker returns scores and optionally a final result list.
[00:01:44] Mark: Quick question — can we use Redwood embeddings but keep vectors in our on-prem FAISS? We have to keep primary copy local for compliance.
[00:01:51] Rachel: Yes, you can. Many customers do that: use hosted embeddings, stream vectors to on-prem FAISS. For privacy, you can use Redwood Private or dedicated tenancy; hosted API also supports VPC peering for private network setups but for strict isolation we'd recommend Private.
[00:02:05] Lina: And are embeddings exempt from being logged? We need to ensure PII is not retained.
[00:02:09] Samir: Good point — we have redaction guidance. For hosted, you can enable request-level retention controls and automatic PII redaction upstream; we also have KMS controls and an option to disable retention entirely per customer. We'll send the security brief after the call.
[00:02:24] Mark: Appreciate that.
[00:02:27] [00:03:00] Jordan: Switching to the Console — I'm sharing my screen. You should see a per-route dashboard with tokens, latencies, and cost breakdown. Over here is Optimize suggestions for reranker — it recommends quantization to int8 for that model class, and shows predicted token cost savings.
[00:03:16] Lina: That prediction looks optimistic. How accurate are those savings?
[00:03:19] Jordan: It's a heuristic based on similar workloads; we run a short profiling job on your corpus during pilot and give a tailored estimate. In our experience it's within 10-20% of actuals.
[00:03:30] Rachel: Also worth noting quantization impacts output slightly — we show a quality delta metric with example outputs so you can verify.
[00:03:37] Devon: How is batching handled? We have spikes with 20k qps in marketing campaigns, but typical is low.
[00:03:42] Samir: The runtime supports continuous batching with request shaping. For spikes we recommend autoscaling and burst capacity; you can also set per-route max batch sizes in the Console. That controls latency vs cost.
[00:03:53] Mark: Can the reranker operate synchronously with top-K = 50 within 150ms p95?
[00:03:58] Rachel: Depends on model choice and hardware. For a mid-sized reranker on our hosted tier, top-K=50 is borderline. We typically recommend retrieving top-100 with a cheap scorer and then rerank top-20 with the stronger model. Or using a lighter reranker architecture.
[00:04:14] Samir: We'll include a latency profile with recommended K values in the follow-up.
[00:04:18] [00:05:00] Jordan: Time for a quick live demo — I'm going to run a batch of 25 sample queries against a sandbox dataset of news articles similar to Crestline's corp. Running /embeddings for index is already done for the sandbox. Now I'll call /search-recall (client-side kNN) and then /rerank.
[00:05:16] [00:05:30] Jordan: (typing) Ok, calling /rerank with top_k=20, scoring model named 'redwood-rerank-v2'. Response coming back...
[00:05:45] Speaker 3: Uh the console is a bit laggy on my side, but I see the request and response times.
[00:05:50] Rachel: The sample shows p50 ~ 70ms, p95 ~ 130ms for the reranker on these inputs, memory usage moderate. You can also enable streaming to see partial scores as they come.
[00:06:02] Mark: Those numbers look promising. What's the per-query cost?
[00:06:06] Samir: Rough ballpark on hosted gen + rerank small model — think on the order of single-digit cents per heavy search if you do per-query rerank; embeddings per-query are a few tenths of a cent if you're batching. We'll run exact pilot numbers.
[00:06:20] Devon: We definitely need concrete pricing for 100k doc pilot and projection to 10M.
[00:06:24] Samir: Understood, will include cost spreadsheet.
[00:06:28] [00:07:00] Rachel: Switching to edge cases — how do you handle query paraphrases and long queries? We often have long product descriptions as queries.
[00:07:06] Jordan: For long queries we recommend truncating or using cross-encoder rerankers which can handle longer context. We also have specialized embedding models tuned for long docs — embedding length affects memory and cost.
[00:07:18] Lina: Any tooling in Optimize to detect regressions? We run A/B tests and need alerts when relevance drops.
[00:07:23] Rachel: Yes, Console has eval set integration. You can upload test prompts and expected answers; metrics are tracked and we send regression alerts when score falls beyond thresholds. We can wire that into your Slack.
[00:07:34] Mark: On compliance: SOC2 + ISO?
[00:07:36] Samir: Redwood is SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 compliant. For audit trails we provide per-request audit logs and optional immutable retention. We'll share the compliance pack.
[00:07:46] Devon: For PII redaction, is there an on-the-fly scrub option? We tried regexes but it's brittle.
[00:07:52] Rachel: We have an optional preprocessor that runs a token-level PII detector and can either redact or hash detected spans before sending to embeddings. For highest assurance customers we recommend Private with customer-managed KMS.
[00:08:07] Lina: If we use hosted embeddings but store vectors on-prem, are embeddings ever materialized in logs?
[00:08:12] Samir: Not if you opt out of retention and enable the no-logs flag. For pilot we'll set that up.
[00:08:18] [00:09:00] Jordan: A brief note on model selection — we have a catalog; for embeddings we recommend mid-sized contextual embeddings for news content (they capture semantics better). For rerankers, we have a family of distilled cross-encoders. The Console shows a quick compare plot of nDCG vs cost.
[00:09:15] Mark: Can we A/B test two models and have Redwood route 10% traffic to a new variant?
[00:09:19] Rachel: Yes. Rollouts in Console support canary and A/B routes, automatic fallback, and experiment metrics.
[00:09:27] [00:10:00] Jordan: Ok running the next demo: I'm toggling quantization suggested by Optimize to int8 on the reranker sandbox to estimate quality delta. This will take a few sec — I'll run a small eval set of 200 queries.
[00:10:18] [00:11:00] Jordan: Results — quality delta shows a 2% nDCG drop but cost savings ~32%. You can inspect individual failure cases; here's a couple where int8 dropped the rerank order.
[00:11:13] Lina: 2% might be acceptable depending on business impact, we need to see top-3 CTR impact.
[00:11:18] Samir: Right, that's why we couple eval sets with real traffic tests during pilot.
[00:11:24] Mark: About scale — for 100k docs what's the onboarding process? How long to index?
[00:11:29] Jordan: Typically indexing 100k documents with embeddings takes a few hours depending on doc size and batch parallelism. We provide ingestion templates and a small SDK script. For larger corpora we recommend a streaming pipeline with checkpointing.
[00:11:41] Devon: Do you have examples or templates for FAISS import?
[00:11:44] Rachel: Yes, we have a repo with sample code to push embeddings to FAISS or other vector DBs. We'll share the link in the notes.
[00:11:51] [00:12:30] Mark: Any competitors we should be aware of for this space? We've looked at some managed vendors and open self-hosted stacks.
[00:12:34] Samir: Customers often compare us with Anthropic/Embeddings vendors and folks who piece together self-hosted runtimes. Key difference is our integrated Console and Optimize with production-grade serving.
[00:12:45] Priya (intern): Quick question — is there a quota for model versions?
[00:12:49] Jordan: You can pin model versions per-route; we support many versions and keep a short retention of old artifacts. For private deployments you control model binaries.
[00:12:58] [00:13:30] Rachel: Ok we have about 15 minutes left — let's capture action items and next steps.
[00:13:35] Mark: Sure.
[00:13:40] Samir: Action items from Redwood: 1) run a 1k query benchmark on Crestline sample dataset and share latency/cost spreadsheet, 2) share security + compliance pack and data retention options, 3) provide FAISS ingestion code and Console access to sandbox. From Crestline: 1) provide sample docs (anonymized) and success metric definitions.
[00:14:02] Lina: We'll prepare an anonymized 10k sample set this week.
[00:14:07] Devon: We'll also send our current reranker eval set.
[00:14:11] Samir: Great. Any final questions?
[00:14:15] Mark: No, that covered it. Good demo.
[00:14:19] Samir: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the materials and proposed pilot plan.
[00:14:24] Rachel: Bye all.
[00:14:26] Mark: Bye.

Note: transcription quality medium — occasional mislabels and background noise on Customer side. Some filler words and shorthand.
